subject: Request: Rollout resilience exception for latency SLOs
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@storix.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@storix.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T18:14:00Z
Subject: Rollout resilience exception for latency SLOs

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo today. We're preparing an A/B launch of Redwood models for our triage assistant (pilot next week) and have one ask before we flip traffic: Storix needs an operational guardrail that will automatically pin traffic back to the previous model variant if 95th percentile latency crosses our agreed SLO (450ms) for more than two minutes.

Specifically we want:
- An automatic fallback rule that re-routes affected sessions to the stable variant when latency breach is detected.
- A temporal pin so the stable variant stays pinned for at least 30 minutes after fallback to avoid oscillation.
- Telemetry hooks and dashboard access so our on-call can see the trigger and reason.

Are you able to approve a short-term exception to Redwood's default canary policy to enable this behavior for the Storix rollout? We've attached a one-page MAP showing rollout timing.

Thanks —
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Integrations, Storix Health
Attachments: storix-mutual-action-plan.pdf
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@storix.com>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@storix.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Rollout resilience exception for latency SLOs

Laura / Aditya —

FYI: Storix has requested a temporary deviation from our standard canary behavior so they can pin back when latency exceeds their SLO. They want both an automated fallback and a temporal pin to prevent flip-flop. This is time-sensitive (pilot next Tue).

Can you confirm the technical feasibility and surface any risk/SLAs we should call out? If this is doable, we need a concise ops playbook and a telem dashboard link we can give them before the pilot.

Proposed quick plan:
1) Define telemetry rule (95p > 450ms for 2 minutes) — Aditya
2) Implement fallback + 30m pin window — Laura
3) Share dashboard + MAP with Storix and sign-off from Legal (if needed) — me

If you can't make the 30m pin, suggest alternatives (e.g., exponential backoff: 10m then 30m) and we'll present options.

- Jonas
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@storix.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Rollout resilience exception for latency SLOs

Jonas / team —

We can implement this with our existing routing and pin primitives; details and caveats below.

Technical proposal (short):
- Trigger: service telemetry fires if 95p inference latency > 450ms for a rolling 2-minute window across the Storix-configured model route.
- Action: automated route override that reassigns 100% of traffic for Storix sessions to the previous stable variant.
- Pin: set variant lock for 30 minutes post-fallback; allow manual override by Ops.
- Rollback criteria: auto-unpin only after 30m and if 95p < 420ms for 10 continuous minutes.

Caveats / ops impact:
- This will create an observable delta in token cost for Storix while pinned to the previous variant (their cost appendix shows expected +8%).
- There is a small window where KV-cache priming on the stable variant may increase tail latency for a few minutes after a fallback.
- Telemetry event will contain: trigger_time, measured_95p, route_id, previous_variant_id, fallback_reason. We can expose those fields to Storix's dashboard link.

Attachments: telemetry-thresholds.csv (detailed numbers).

If Legal wants an explicit waiver around SLO-driven fallbacks for the pilot, let me know and I can draft the short clause. From Ops side this is low-risk if we: 1) enable manual abort for auto-fallback, and 2) provide a rollback playbook.

Laura
Sr PM, Release Reliability
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@storix.com>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@storix.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Rollout resilience exception for latency SLOs — APPROVED (pilot guardrails)

Sarah / Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask and the MAP. We've reviewed with Release Reliability and SRE. Approved for the pilot with the following binding guardrails: 

- Trigger: 95p > 450ms for 2 continuous minutes will initiate an automatic fallback to the previous stable variant.
- Pin window: 30 minutes after fallback; manual unpin by Storix Ops only if coordinated with Redwood on-call.
- Auto-unpin: only if 95p < 420ms sustained for 10 minutes after the pin window.
- Ops controls: Redwood will expose a one-click manual abort and an events feed (trigger_time, measured_95p, route_id, previous_variant_id).

Please find the MAP and thresholds attached. We'll add a one-paragraph addendum to the contract (pilot exception) — Legal will send it to you in a separate thread; signing expected today.

Next steps for Storix:
1) Confirm pilot start time (we'll hold final config until 24 hours before).
2) Provide the list of route IDs you plan to flip.
3) Confirm who should receive the event feed (Ops emails).

If anything changes, loop me in and we'll pause the rollout.

Thanks —
Jonas
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachments: storix-mutual-action-plan.pdf, storix-technical-appendix.docx
